title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet

selection.evidence: MASS opens on it: 'self-feedback can reinforce rather than correct errors (Huang et al., 2024)'. Read to check how strong that premise is.

cost.compute_notes: 17-page PDF, Secs 1-5 and Tables 1-8 read. h01 under 1 s. No code needed: Figure 1 carries the paired transitions.

triggers: multi-agent debate vs self-consistency equal responses

claims.statement: Without oracle labels (intrinsic self-correction), accuracy drops for all models on all benchmarks after self-correction; prior gains came from using the gold label to decide when to stop.
claims.scope: GSM8K, CommonSenseQA, HotpotQA; GPT-3.5 (full sets), GPT-4, GPT-4-Turbo, Llama-2-70b-chat (200 sampled questions); two rounds; three feedback prompts for GPT-4-Turbo and Llama-2.

quantities.name: cells_with_significant_drop_mcnemar
quantities.unit: model x task cells, exact McNemar p < 0.05 on Fig 1 transitions

our_assessment.why: Transitions reproduce every table delta exactly (8/8). The sign holds everywhere, so self-correction never helps here. But the drop is large and significant only where the model is weak or the task is suggestible: Llama-2 on both tasks, GPT-3.5 on CommonSenseQA, GPT-4 on GSM8K. For GPT-4-Turbo on both tasks, GPT-4 on CommonSenseQA and GPT-3.5 on GSM8K, the change is indistinguishable from zero (p 0.31-0.83). The defensible claim is: 'intrinsic self-correction does not improve, and degrades models that lack confidence'. 'Drops for all' over-reads four null cells. For MASS this cuts both ways: a strong self-judge may simply be inert rather than harmful.

claims.statement: Multi-agent debate does not beat self-consistency at an equal number of responses: on full GSM8K (gpt-3.5-turbo-0301), debate with 9 responses 83.0% vs majority vote over 9 samples 88.2%; debate's gain is 'consistency', not 'correction'.

our_assessment.why: Large and well-powered on the full test set. It is the earliest instance in this area of the equal-compute baseline argument (later wang2026, tran2026).

claims.statement: Self-Refine's constrained-generation gain disappears when the initial prompt contains the requirements that the feedback prompt adds: standard prompting with a better prompt gets 81.8 vs 75.1 after self-correction.

our_assessment.why: The pattern is that the 'improvement' was an instruction-placement confound in the baseline. It is the same shape as RHI's optimiser prompt that predetermines 'contracts and hops'.

checked.result: All 8 transition sets sum to 100 and reproduce the Standard -> round-2 deltas of Tables 3-4.

open_questions: Does the null effect for strong models hold at larger n? 200 questions only exclude drops above about 4 pp.
